rubric_content.text_property: The response groups emails into distinct priority categories including at minimum Urgent and Action Needed.

rubrics.description: This is the core behavior the case exists to catch: that classification_agent's involvement actually produced categorized output, not a flat list.

rubric_content.text_property: Verification codes and security alerts (e.g. a new sign-in, password reset, or account compromise warning) are NOT categorised as Urgent, even when they mention expiring soon.

rubrics.description: Urgent means the user's job search needs action now, not general time-sensitivity. A verification code or security alert requires no job-search action, however soon it expires.

rubric_content.text_property: Every email categorised as Urgent, if any, is a job-search matter requiring action from the user, such as an interview scheduling request, an assessment or take-home with a due date, or an application requiring information by a deadline.

rubrics.description: Guards against generic time-sensitivity (expiring codes, account alerts) being treated as Urgent instead of job-search deadlines.

rubric_content.text_property: Two emails of the same kind (e.g. two verification codes) are categorised consistently with each other, not split across different categories.

rubrics.description: Guards against the same kind of email landing in different categories within one response, which indicates the classification rule was applied inconsistently rather than derived from a stable rule.

rubric_content.text_property: Job rejections, job recommendations, marketing emails, verification codes and security alerts are NOT categorised as Action Needed.

rubrics.description: Guards against over-eager classification treating no-action correspondence as requiring a response.

rubric_content.text_property: The response accounts for all emails, either individually or by stating a count of remaining lower-priority ones.

rubrics.description: Guards against silently dropping emails that don't fall into a highlighted category.
